summary: Establishes the explicit Year One digital product team and lean shared capability needed to deliver King’s Edge, support the focused first Digital Student Experience Hub release and learn what enduring digital product capability King’s requires.
detailSummary:
Digital Innovation and Product Development Capability establishes the team and working practices through which King’s Edge and the first Digital Student Experience Hub release are delivered. During 2026/27, the capability itself is part of the discovery: King’s tests how much core capacity is needed, which specialist inputs must be reliably available, and which product and operating practices are required for sustainable delivery.

The Year One funded core is 4.0 FTE across four explicit posts, each with its own planning cost for November 2026 to June 2027. The Senior Backend & Integration Engineer (1.0 FTE) owns backend services, domain/API integration, technical integration with King’s systems and senior engineering judgement; the planning assumption is King’s Grade 8 midpoint and approximately £61,000 including employer on-costs. The Middleweight Full-Stack Engineer (1.0 FTE) provides hands-on delivery across the student-facing Hub, King’s Edge and supporting application services; the planning assumption is Grade 7 midpoint and approximately £50,000 including employer on-costs. The Product & Service Designer (1.0 FTE) combines UX and interaction design, UI design, service and journey design, prototyping, student/user research and usability testing; the planning assumption is Grade 7 midpoint and approximately £50,000 including employer on-costs. The QA Engineer (1.0 FTE) owns product test strategy, automated and manual quality assurance, regression and release quality; the planning assumption is Grade 6 midpoint and approximately £42,000 including employer on-costs. The QA estimate assumes the same eight-month planning period for a conservative baseline, although a later start once code production is established would reduce actual spend. These four role estimates replace the previous global staffing holding envelope and total approximately £203,000. Digital and IT / HR must validate final grades, appointment points and start dates before the business case is finalised.

Mark Peace is the Product Owner during mobilisation, so no additional Product Owner post or fractional allocation is required in the resource model. The four funded posts are supported by a deliberately small amount of shared institutional capacity: approximately 0.2 FTE Business Analyst during the main discovery period to map systems, information flows, ownership, dependencies and operational readiness; approximately 0.2 FTE DevOps/platform support from Digital and IT for Azure, environments, deployment pipelines and observability; and up to approximately 0.2 FTE solution architecture only if the Senior Backend & Integration Engineer cannot credibly carry that function. Specialist security, privacy, accessibility, data, architecture assurance and service-management input is drawn from existing institutional functions when required rather than represented as standing fractional posts. Product quality assurance remains the responsibility of the QA Engineer.

The substantive build demand remains King’s Edge, with the same team establishing the reusable Hub foundations and focused first-release experience under 4.1.2. The Year One baseline includes a £90,000 planning allowance for ring-fenced agentic software-development tooling so the experienced engineering team can test and use agentic development as a material productivity accelerator. The amount is based on the 28 August Digital and IT discussion and remains subject to commercial validation, including whether existing shared capacity can reduce the eventual cost. It is budgeted separately from the £50,000 Azure/environment/platform envelope. The existing KAI team is not assumed to transfer wholesale into the capability, but reusable technical assets, including Azure AI Foundry components, should be assessed and adopted where they fit the target architecture.

The current Year One cash baseline across 4.1.2 and 4.1.3 is approximately £358,000: £203,000 across the four individually costed product-team posts, £50,000 Azure/environments/platform, £15,000 paid student co-design and £90,000 agentic software-development tooling. By the end of Year One, King’s should have both delivered product capability and evidence about the capability model itself. Actual throughput, quality, discovery demand, integration effort, specialist dependencies, tooling productivity and live-service obligations should determine the team shape and investment required in Years Two and Three.

caseForChange.problem:
King’s does not currently have a sufficiently dependable multidisciplinary product capability for turning emerging student-experience needs into working, supported digital services at pace. Requirements can be addressed through conventional system change, local initiatives, temporary projects or standalone products, making prioritisation and reuse difficult.

King’s now needs enough in-house capability to deliver a substantial King’s Edge roadmap and establish the first Digital Student Experience Hub foundations, while also supporting broader discovery of the student digital estate. The precise enduring team shape is not yet known well enough to justify fixing it in advance.
caseForChange.opportunity:
An explicit four-post funded product core, combined with a lean shared Business Analysis, DevOps/platform and conditional solution-architecture model, gives King’s a disciplined route from need to supported change without overcomplicating the team. Combining UX/UI, service design and user research in the Product & Service Designer keeps discovery close to product delivery, while dedicated QA protects release quality. Ring-fenced agentic software-development tooling gives the experienced engineering team a practical way to test whether agentic development can materially increase throughput without weakening engineering judgement or quality.

King’s Edge supplies the first substantive product demand. The Digital Student Experience Hub extends that work into reusable shared foundations and a focused institutional release, while broad discovery informs the next phase.
caseForChange.whyNow:
King’s Edge creates an immediate requirement for dependable in-house digital product delivery. At the same time, the Digital Student Experience Hub needs a focused September 2027 first release and a wider evidence base for the remainder of the mobilisation.

2026/27 is therefore the right point to mobilise the four funded posts, secure the small shared capacities they depend on, fund and test agentic development as part of the engineering model and learn through real delivery. Future expansion should follow evidence about throughput, journey demand, integration complexity, quality and operational load.
caseForChange.intendedChange:
King’s has a dependable multidisciplinary digital product capability with a transparent pipeline, clear decision rights and repeatable practices for discovery, design, engineering, quality, assurance, release and continuous improvement.

During 2026/27, the funded 4.0 FTE core delivers the King’s Edge replatform and agreed product roadmap and supports the focused first Digital Student Experience Hub release. Each funded post is costed separately in the Year One model rather than hidden beneath a generic staffing envelope. Mark Peace acts as Product Owner. The Product & Service Designer combines UX/UI, service design and user research. Shared institutional support is kept deliberately lean: approximately 0.2 FTE Business Analysis, approximately 0.2 FTE DevOps/platform support, and up to approximately 0.2 FTE solution architecture only if the senior engineering role cannot absorb it, with specialist assurance drawn on demand. A £90,000 planning allowance provides ring-fenced agentic software-development tooling for the Year One engineering model.

The capability can then expand or change shape where live demand and evidence justify it, with future staffing, tooling and recurrent costs confirmed through the wider three-year mobilisation business case rather than carried forward as automatic assumptions.

benefits.title: King’s responds more quickly to emerging student needs
benefits.statement: Priority needs can be translated into tested digital responses in shorter cycles, with student and staff evidence shaping development before large commitments are made.
benefits.realisationPeriod: From establishment of the first delivery pipeline
benefits.successLooksLike: Priority needs move predictably from discovery to evaluated live use, and users can influence solutions while they remain adaptable.

benefits.title: Digital delivery becomes more predictable and evidence-led
benefits.statement: A transparent pipeline, explicit capacity decisions and consistent product and assurance practices make needs, priorities, progress and trade-offs clearer.
benefits.beneficiary: Students, service owners, Digital and IT and King’s
benefits.realisationPeriod: As the operating model becomes routine
benefits.successLooksLike: Demand is prioritised through one route, delivery commitments are visible and changes in team capacity can be explained by actual roadmap evidence.

benefits.title: Successful innovation becomes sustainable institutional provision
benefits.statement: Valuable changes have a defined route into secure, supported and appropriately owned operation, while multidisciplinary capability remains available for continuous improvement.
benefits.beneficiary: Students, service owners, Digital and IT and King’s
benefits.successLooksLike: Successful capabilities have explicit ownership and support arrangements, unsuccessful trials close cleanly, and the product capability has an evidence-based route into business as usual.

steps.title: Recruit and mobilise the core multidisciplinary digital product team
steps.summary: From September through November 2026, secure funding and recruit or assign four explicit Year One posts through Digital and IT: 1.0 FTE Senior Backend & Integration Engineer at a planning cost of approximately £61,000, 1.0 FTE Middleweight Full-Stack Engineer at approximately £50,000, 1.0 FTE Product & Service Designer at approximately £50,000 and 1.0 FTE QA Engineer at approximately £42,000 for the November-to-June Year One period. Confirm final grading and appointment points with Digital and IT / HR. Confirm Mark Peace as Product Owner, approximately 0.2 FTE protected Business Analysis, approximately 0.2 FTE DevOps/platform support, and up to approximately 0.2 FTE solution architecture only if not covered by the senior engineering post. Confirm the commercial route for the £90,000 ring-fenced agentic software-development tooling allowance.

steps.title: Establish the product operating model and delivery practices
steps.summary: From November 2026 to February 2027, establish one transparent pipeline, prioritisation and capacity cadence, proportionate discovery and user involvement, engineering and quality expectations, agentic-development practices, embedded assurance and release practices across King’s Edge and the Digital Student Experience Hub.

steps.title: Prove the capability through King’s Edge, broad discovery and the focused Hub release
steps.summary: From January to October 2027, prove that the funded core and lean shared-capacity model can deliver the substantive King’s Edge roadmap and focused Digital Student Experience Hub release while the Product & Service Designer leads integrated experience discovery and design. Measure the contribution of agentic development alongside quality and rework, and use evidence to identify real capacity gaps before expanding the team.

steps.title: Make product operations and live-service collaboration routine
steps.summary: From November 2027 to February 2028, make operating practices routine across the live Digital Student Experience Hub and King’s Edge product domain, balancing roadmap delivery, incidents, maintenance, quality, discovery and continuous improvement.

steps.title: Scale the team and its practices where the wider roadmap justifies it
steps.summary: From March to October 2028, expand or reshape the core and specialist capability only where live-service evidence, broad discovery and the confirmed wider student-journey roadmap justify additional throughput or expertise.

steps.title: Embed an enduring institutional product-development capability
steps.summary: By the end of the three-year mobilisation, establish the sustainable multidisciplinary capability, professional leadership, governance, product practices and interfaces with SED product ownership and Digital and IT specialist/platform services. Confirm recurrent staffing, tooling and costs from live evidence before business-as-usual transition.
